notice: Candidate score rules are not production approvals. Every score rule requires scientific and runtime review.

rules.condition: Late summer/early autumn estuarine yellow eels: just after sunset through night
rules.mechanism: Baited capture began immediately after sunset and was overwhelmingly nocturnal.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not double count sunset, underwater light and clock time; restrict season/waterbody/life stage.

rules.condition: Chronic acclimation at or below about 5 C for more than five weeks
rules.mechanism: Winter torpor suppressed feeding and metabolism.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not apply to a brief cold front or infer exact field temperature without acclimation history.

rules.condition: 10-20 C acclimated laboratory conditions
rules.mechanism: Eels fed regularly across this range.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Presence of feeding is not a positive curve or maximum.

rules.condition: Final preferendum near 16.7 C
rules.mechanism: Selected temperature measured habitat choice only.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not conflate preference with appetite.

rules.condition: Colder months in lower Chesapeake trawls
rules.mechanism: Trawl catches declined as water cooled.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Abundance, depth, activity and gear encounter are confounded.

rules.condition: Unusually concentrated prey available in daylight
rules.mechanism: Eels can feed during day when prey pulses overwhelm normal diel pattern.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: No generic daytime bonus; requires observed prey event.

rules.condition: Any tide direction
rules.mechanism: Telemetry showed tidal movement, not feeding/catchability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer bite from movement.

rules.condition: Seasonal movement with discharge changes
rules.mechanism: Flow helped explain migration/movement in the Shenandoah.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Movement and access are separate from feeding.

rules.condition: Confirmed downstream-migrating silver stage
rules.mechanism: Digestive regression and migration reduce feeding.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Life stage cannot be inferred from month alone.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct endpoint evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Reject folklore and migration-only associations.

rules.condition: Any threshold
rules.mechanism: No portable direct feeding/hook-and-line threshold qualified.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not use habitat/tolerance evidence.

rules.condition: 26–32 cm total length within populations and gear contexts comparable to the five-reservoir tagging study
rules.mechanism: Angler returns peaked in this measured size band.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not extrapolate beyond 20.0–39.8 cm, duplicate retention/gear selectivity, or treat as a physiological optimum.

rules.condition: Near 20 cm or above approximately 32 cm within the measured 20.0–39.8 cm range
rules.mechanism: Tagged-fish return probability was lower at the small and large ends of the observed range.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Use a bounded categorical calibration candidate, not a smooth universal curve.

rules.condition: 0–50 NTU for juvenile black crappie under the tested prey and light conditions
rules.mechanism: Foraging did not collapse across the tested range.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not interpret null impairment as a turbidity benefit or transfer to adults and lures.

rules.condition: Black crappie phenotype in Weiss Reservoir versus white crappie and natural hybrids
rules.mechanism: Black crappie were overrepresented in angler catch relative to independent sampling.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not encode a universal species bonus across waters.

rules.condition: Dissolved oxygen below 2 mg/L, temperature at or below 1°C, or current above about 1 cm/s in winter backwaters
rules.mechanism: Fish relocated to trade off oxygen, temperature, and current.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Movement/habitat selection is not feeding; do not score exact thresholds outside winter backwaters.

rules.condition: Any universal daytime or nighttime category
rules.mechanism: One Ontario study found July nighttime return to feeding habitat, but diel behavior is waterbody and season dependent.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not stack clock time with underwater light, prey movement, and habitat occupancy.

rules.condition: Spring and early-summer staging, nesting, and male guarding
rules.mechanism: Reproduction changes location and may produce defense without proving increased feeding.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not label nest defense as feeding or add a generic spring bonus.

rules.condition: Any direct atmospheric or solunar multiplier
rules.mechanism: No qualifying species-specific direct evidence was found.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Prefer measured aquatic conditions; do not double count weather-mediated temperature, light, flow, or oxygen.

rules.condition: Any numerical short-term learning or depletion curve
rules.mechanism: Available studies do not separate learning from removal, density, effort, and size selectivity.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer pressure decay from declining catch alone.

rules.condition: Summer conditions comparable to the reviewed Lake Ontario tributary
rules.direction: Increase expected feeding near crepuscular periods; main observed peak 1600-2000 h and smaller peak 0400-0800 h
rules.mechanism: Direct diel feeding periodicity from stomach-content evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: High risk of double counting light, season, temperature, and local prey timing. Do not apply outside summer or as a universal hourly curve.

rules.condition: Where benthic chironomids/mayflies are locally available
rules.direction: Guide presentation and prey matching; no calibrated bonus
rules.mechanism: Diet and benthos association.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting substrate and stream productivity.

rules.condition: Water declining below 5.0 C in a comparable stream
rules.direction: Shift location context toward rubble crevices and winter focal habitat
rules.mechanism: Observed seasonal habitat shift.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not translate habitat shift into lower or higher feeding.

rules.condition: Population-specific home-stream current regime
rules.direction: Use as transfer and habitat context only
rules.mechanism: Swimming performance and plasticity vary among populations.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not treat high swimming performance as high bite activity.

rules.condition: Studies west of Appalachians or labeled western blacknose dace
rules.direction: Require taxonomic review before transfer to NOVA R. atratulus
rules.mechanism: Modern molecular evidence separates R. atratulus and R. obtusus.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Prevents mixing species/population effects.

rules.condition: 29.9 C versus 28.8 C lethal-tolerance result
rules.mechanism: The experiment measured lethality/resistance, not ingestion.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting temperature and photoperiod as feeding.

rules.condition: Juvenile artificial-stream predator experiment
rules.mechanism: Anti-predator space use is not feeding.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid converting avoidance behavior to catchability.

rules.condition: Approximately 5 C versus 15-25 C under the Schmitt laboratory design
rules.direction: decrease below 15 C relative to tested warmer treatments
rules.mechanism: Cold water reduced maximum daily ration; 15 and 25 C were not significantly different.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not declare 15 C an optimum, interpolate a smooth curve, or double count season.

rules.condition: 840-890 mm in sampled Missouri River reaches or 891-1,015 mm in sampled Mississippi River reaches
rules.direction: increase in observed exploitation relative to other sampled sizes
rules.mechanism: Angler selectivity and vulnerability produced size-specific return patterns.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Highly fishery-specific; avoid treating as innate appetite or transferring exact bins to NOVA without local tagging/creel data.

rules.condition: Gizzard shad versus blue crab under laboratory maximum-ration trials
rules.mechanism: Prey form and handling affected intake.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Fish Guide/forage context; do not double count prey abundance and fish size.

rules.condition: Near end of outgoing tide in three sampled rivers, but incoming tide in the Mattaponi
rules.mechanism: Tidal transport and prey access may affect feeding chronology.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Contradictory river result; no universal outgoing-tide bonus.

rules.condition: Clock hour alone
rules.mechanism: Peak times differed among rivers despite an overall 0900-1500 fullness window.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting tide, prey, temperature and sampling schedule.

rules.condition: Tidal fresh, oligohaline or mesohaline zone
rules.mechanism: Salinity co-varied with prey community and habitat.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer feeding intensity or catchability from occupancy.

rules.condition: Tributary use or flood-associated movement
rules.mechanism: Telemetry measured movement and access, not feeding.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting flow, season and reproduction.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct species-specific evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Folklore is not evidence.

rules.condition: Calendar month alone
rules.mechanism: Seasonal diet and habitat shifts do not establish intrinsic monthly catchability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting temperature, prey, salinity, access and effort.

rules.condition: Intermittent nighttime artificial light at 12 lx, matching the juvenile mesocosm treatment
rules.mechanism: Flashing/intermittent high-intensity light reduced strike and prey-capture rates.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Restrict to artificial intermittent illumination; do not generalize to moon, clouds, steady lights, adults, or natural waters.

rules.condition: Steady nighttime artificial light at 1, 4, or 12 lx in juvenile mesocosms
rules.mechanism: No apparent effect on the measured foraging metrics.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer neutrality at other spectra/intensities or under different cover and prey.

rules.condition: Larval conditions where sediment turbidity coincides with underwater light below roughly 450 lx
rules.mechanism: Consumption declined under the combined low-light/turbidity condition.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Larval-only; do not score adults or create a universal NTU threshold.

rules.condition: Population- and setting-specific behavioral phenotype
rules.mechanism: Angled versus seined fish differed in timidity, but direction changed in a second experiment.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Contradictory setting effects prohibit a universal personality bonus.

rules.condition: More sociable individuals in the studied pond
rules.mechanism: Sociable Bluegill were selectively captured.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Trait is not observable from public environmental data and may covary with group location.

rules.condition: Aggression or dominance phenotype
rules.mechanism: No similarly clear capture association was supported in the reviewed sociability study.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not substitute nesting aggression for general feeding catchability.

rules.condition: Standard or maximum metabolic rate, postexercise oxygen use, or recovery time in the studied fish
rules.mechanism: Captured and uncaptured Bluegill did not differ.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer individual metabolic state from ambient temperature or weather.

rules.condition: Dissolved oxygen below 2 mg/L, temperature at or below 1°C, or current above about 1 cm/s in winter backwaters
rules.mechanism: Fish altered habitat selection to balance oxygen, temperature, and current.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Movement is not feeding or angling; thresholds are winter backwater-specific.

rules.condition: Age-0 fish at 4°C versus 9°C with food present/absent and 20–30 versus 50–60 mm size classes
rules.mechanism: Consumption and survival depended jointly on temperature, food, size, and condition.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not use juvenile survival/feeding as an adult bite optimum.

rules.condition: Early-summer colonies and male guarding
rules.mechanism: Local vulnerability can reflect defense rather than feeding.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not stack with generic summer, shallow-water, or aggression bonuses.

rules.condition: Any direct atmospheric or natural-lunar multiplier
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct Bluegill evidence was found; artificial-light evidence is not a surrogate.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting measured underwater light, temperature, flow, and oxygen.

rules.condition: Any short-term learning/depletion curve
rules.mechanism: Individual vulnerability is selective, but no portable pressure-decay function was identified.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer learning from falling catch without accounting for removals and effort.

rules.condition: 18-22 C with creek chub present in the Colby flow-through-tank design
rules.mechanism: Warming weakened brook-trout feeding and aggression under interspecific competition.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Requires competitor presence; avoid double counting temperature, species composition, aggression and habitat displacement; no smooth curve.

rules.condition: East Branch Fox versus Au Sable strains in the Michigan exploitation experiment
rules.mechanism: Inherited or learned strain differences in growth/behavior affected angling vulnerability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not map to Virginia lineages without genetic/stocking provenance; growth and behavior are confounded.

rules.condition: <3 to >40 NTU at 12 C, 49 lx and 0.06 m/s for juvenile hatchery fish
rules.mechanism: Fish maintained intake by increasing activity and changing search strategy.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer no effect on adult catchability, energy balance, higher turbidity or different light/current.

rules.condition: 1-30 days after stocking in Virginia pooled trout data
rules.mechanism: Catch did not show a simple monotonic post-stocking decline.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Pooled species and overlapping stocking/harvest.

rules.condition: Actual stocking day
rules.mechanism: Immediate concentration and accessibility.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: May be access rather than feeding; pooled species.

rules.condition: Warm mainstem with accessible cold-water refuge
rules.direction: increase in local encounter/catch concentration, not appetite
rules.mechanism: Fish aggregate in refuge patches under heat.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not score warm water as beneficial or double count occupancy and ethical heat stress.

rules.condition: Any universal bite threshold derived from activity or occupancy
rules.mechanism: Available brook-trout oxygen studies measured distribution or activity, not feeding/catchability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not substitute habitat choice for bite probability.

rules.condition: Day/night/light category from lake telemetry
rules.mechanism: Movement and depth changed, but feeding and hook-and-line capture were not measured.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not transfer an ice-covered lake schedule to Appalachian streams.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No direct species-specific feeding or catchability evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not proxy temperature, light or flow with folklore.

rules.condition: Calendar month alone
rules.mechanism: Native versus stocked populations, spawning, access and temperature differ too much for a universal curve.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting season, stocking and effort.

rules.condition: After sustained acclimation: compare approximately 25 C with 18 C
rules.strength: strong within study; do not calibrate universally
rules.mechanism: Attack rate fell, handling time rose, and modeled maximum consumption declined after long acclimation.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: High risk of double-counting season, warm-water stress, and prey availability. Use categorical evidence gate, not a smooth curve.

rules.condition: Within the studied cold range, 3 C to 4.5 C
rules.mechanism: Small warming increased modeled consumption in a juvenile European winter experiment.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not combine with a general temperature curve or treat 4.5 C as an optimum.

rules.condition: Winter lab conditions comparable to the reviewed experiment
rules.mechanism: Actual prey consumption was overwhelmingly nocturnal in the winter experiment.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Double-counting risk with cover, clarity, season, and temperature; do not universalize to summer.

rules.condition: Approximately 2-3 C
rules.direction: suppress expected feeding but never force a universal zero
rules.mechanism: A field comparison found no stomach feeding near 2 C, but a controlled experiment documented predation at 3 C.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Contradictory designs and populations; use only to prevent a false hard cessation threshold.

rules.condition: Any uncalibrated natural flow condition
rules.mechanism: Flow altered odor-source localization in a flume.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not double count flow with turbidity or prey delivery; no ingestion endpoint.

rules.condition: When chironomids, amphipods, detritus, or fish prey availability changes
rules.mechanism: Field diets were opportunistic and habitat dependent.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not make prey abundance an automatic feeding-rate bonus without local prey data.

rules.condition: 18 C versus 25 C experimental treatments
rules.mechanism: Condition and feeding efficiency did not move identically.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Prevents double counting physiology as bite score.

rules.condition: Any growth-optimum estimate
rules.mechanism: Growth endpoint is not feeding or catchability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting temperature and life stage.

rules.condition: Fish caught/released or closely disturbed during the previous several days in clear, sight-fished backcountry rivers
rules.mechanism: Learning, displacement and increased wariness reduce approachability and repeat vulnerability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not assume a universal duration; avoid double counting effort, fish depletion, access and visibility.

rules.condition: Approximately 450-600 mg/L in the Greer experimental design
rules.mechanism: Extreme suspended sediment interfered with prey acquisition even though respiration was not similarly reduced.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not convert mg/L to NTU or extrapolate a smooth curve to ordinary stain.

rules.condition: 1-30 days after stocking in Virginia pooled put-and-take data
rules.mechanism: Catch stayed near the managerial target after the initial pulse.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Species were pooled; local stocking overlap and harvest remain confounders.

rules.condition: Actual stocking day
rules.mechanism: Immediate accessibility and concentrated fish.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: May reflect access and effort rather than feeding; pooled species.

rules.condition: High exploratory behavior in hatchery-reared fish
rules.mechanism: Behavioral phenotype affected capture vulnerability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Personality is usually unobserved and may be altered by stocking history.

rules.condition: Absolute temperature with body size and ration known
rules.mechanism: Feeding capacity is jointly controlled by temperature, body mass and ration.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not convert a growth or lab feeding equation into catchability or double count season.

rules.condition: Sunrise, sunset or night based only on telemetry movement
rules.mechanism: Seasonal movement timing was measured, not feeding or hook-and-line capture.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not equate movement with biting.

rules.condition: Winter month alone
rules.mechanism: Field evidence shows continued winter feeding in a stable groundwater stream.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Does not imply high catchability; local temperature and prey remain important.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct species-specific evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer from movement or angler folklore.

rules.condition: Calendar month alone
rules.mechanism: Telemetry, spawning and stocking schedules do not establish intrinsic monthly bite probability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting temperature, access, regulations and effort.

rules.condition: Progressive cooling from summer toward winter within the population's recent thermal history
rules.mechanism: Regional stomach data and controlled winter feeding both show declining consumption as water cools, while feeding persists at low temperatures.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not add independent month, winter, photoperiod, and temperature penalties for the same seasonal mechanism.

rules.condition: Cooling day versus warming or thermally stable day during cold-water conditions
rules.mechanism: Winter feed intake was lower on cooling days than on warming or unchanged days within the studied managed-pond range.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not relabel this as a cold-front or barometric-pressure effect; use measured water-temperature trend only.

rules.condition: Sustained cyclic water temperature reaching 31-35 C (87.8-95 F)
rules.mechanism: Juvenile feed consumption declined in the hottest treatment even as general activity increased, consistent with heat stress rather than inactivity.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not set 27-31 C as a wild bite optimum or separately stack heat, summer, and oxygen penalties without measured inputs.

rules.condition: Declining oxygen saturation below well-oxygenated conditions, especially near 36% or lower in the studied experiments
rules.mechanism: Feed intake declined progressively with oxygen saturation, and food consumption was severely reduced at 36% saturation despite survival.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not convert percent saturation to a fixed mg/L value without water temperature, pressure, and salinity.

rules.condition: Warm pond or reservoir nightly minimum below approximately 3.0 mg/L, with stronger penalty below 2.5 mg/L
rules.mechanism: Commercial-pond feed consumption declined as minimum daily oxygen fell, with a nonlinear loss at severe minima.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Use only where a comparable warmwater nightly minimum is measured; do not combine blindly with percent-saturation rule.

rules.condition: Same day or first daily fishing period after a documented put-and-take Channel Catfish stocking
rules.mechanism: Newly stocked harvestable Channel Catfish were exceptionally accessible immediately after stocking; catch declined sharply by the next daily survey.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Restrict to managed stocked ponds and avoid stacking with abundance or generic seasonal bonuses. The mechanism is accessibility and depletion, not proven feeding.

rules.condition: Any universal night, dawn, or afternoon category
rules.mechanism: Adult Mid-Atlantic stomach data indicated strong daylight and afternoon feeding, whereas river telemetry and juvenile work indicated nocturnal behavior.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not use time of day independently from life stage, waterbody, season, cover, and actual underwater light.

rules.condition: Elevated flow reconnects channel, floodplain, oxbow, or backwater habitat
rules.mechanism: Adults relocated into newly connected floodplain and oxbow habitat during elevated flow.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not translate movement into increased feeding or reuse Mississippi discharge values in Northern Virginia.

rules.condition: April-June Virginia cavity spawning and male guarding
rules.mechanism: Spawning and male nest defense may change location and behavior, but no direct angling-catchability study of guarding Channel Catfish was identified.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not copy black-bass nest-defense catchability to Channel Catfish.

rules.condition: Unknown hatchery strain, crossbreed, or Channel x Blue hybrid contribution
rules.mechanism: Genetic groups differed in angling vulnerability in controlled studies.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not assume every Virginia stocking consists of a single known strain or pure Channel Catfish unless stocking records confirm it.

rules.condition: Pennsylvania reservoir July-October or river June-September catch concentration
rules.mechanism: Creel catches were concentrated in warm months but reflect effort, abundance, access, and sampling design as well as fish behavior.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not stack seasonal catch context with measured temperature and stocking effects.

rules.condition: Any direct weather or solunar rule
rules.mechanism: No qualifying species-specific study isolated these variables after aquatic mediators were controlled.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Model measured water temperature, oxygen, flow, turbidity, and stocking rather than atmospheric folklore.

rules.condition: Chronic or acclimated conditions near 6 C versus 14-28 C
rules.direction: strong negative at 6 C; higher at intermediate/warm treatments
rules.mechanism: Voluntary ration was nearly suppressed at 6 C and rose sharply by 14 C.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not double count season or short-term trend; exact strain and feeding regime matter.

rules.condition: Juveniles at 16 C versus 20-28 C
rules.direction: lower feeding at 16 C; plateau around 24-28 C
rules.mechanism: Temperature altered juvenile functional response and intake.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Juvenile laboratory result must not be merged with adult ration percentages as one curve.

rules.condition: 34 C relative to 28 C in the ration experiment
rules.mechanism: Daily ration declined at the hottest treatment.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not treat 34 C as a sharp field cutoff; oxygen and acclimation may co-vary.

rules.condition: Approximately 08:00-11:00 and 19:00-23:00 under the tested husbandry
rules.mechanism: Repeated diel peaks in voluntary feed intake.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Clock time, photoperiod, feeding schedule and temperature are confounded.

rules.condition: Direct catch-and-release within hours to about one week
rules.mechanism: Private learning produced short-term hook/rig avoidance.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting recent pressure, individual capture history and population depletion.

rules.condition: Witnessing conspecific capture within hours/days
rules.mechanism: Social information induced temporary caution.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Only use where local pressure/group exposure can be proxied; effect was less persistent.

rules.condition: More than seven months after one exposure
rules.mechanism: Long-term retest did not reproduce durable one-trial avoidance.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Does not negate shorter learning or repeated-capture effects.

rules.condition: Domesticated versus wild-type ancestry
rules.mechanism: Domestication and boldness changed vulnerability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Ancestry is usually unknown and should not be inferred from body shape alone.

rules.condition: Repeated familiar bait at a fixed site
rules.mechanism: Conditioning can aggregate fish and increase bait acceptance.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Belongs in Fish Guide, not weather score.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Reject folklore and effort-confounded competition data.

rules.condition: Any mg/L threshold from tolerance studies
rules.mechanism: No direct feeding/catchability coefficient qualified.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer from survival or habitat occupancy.

rules.condition: Summer in comparable small streams: early evening versus morning
rules.mechanism: Field stomach-content data showed greatest feeding intensity in early evening.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not double count sunset, terrestrial insect input and season.

rules.condition: Later versus earlier summer in the Minnesota study
rules.mechanism: Observed feeding intensity declined over the sampled summer.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Prey, temperature and sampling date are confounded; no monthly curve.

rules.condition: 18-22 C with brook trout present, or broader 3-26 C paired trials
rules.mechanism: Temperature shifted competitive feeding and aggression.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Requires competitor identity/abundance; do not apply as simple temperature score.

rules.condition: Any single-species optimum inferred from competition experiments
rules.mechanism: No clean single-species response qualified.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting trout stress and competitive release.

rules.condition: More than 15 cm/s at shallow spawning sites
rules.mechanism: Measured condition described spawning habitat.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Not a bite or feeding threshold.

rules.condition: Available covered habitat patches in low-gradient streams
rules.mechanism: Creek chub moved among patches and used cover.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Movement is not appetite.

rules.condition: Any threshold
rules.mechanism: No direct feeding/catchability evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not use tolerance classifications.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Reject folklore.

rules.condition: Fixed monthly curve
rules.mechanism: No direct monthly curve.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Separate diel, spawn and prey processes.

rules.condition: Small artificial lures and trout-sized offerings
rules.mechanism: Regional agencies document deliberate captures.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Not an environmental multiplier.

rules.condition: Summer, comparable river habitat: late-day/evening relative to other sampled diel intervals
rules.mechanism: A field stomach-content study found a distinct diel feeding peak.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not double count sunset, terrestrial-insect fall, season and water clarity.

rules.condition: Locally concentrated energy-rich prey such as exposed eggs or newly emerged small fish
rules.mechanism: Fallfish exploited exceptional salmon egg/parr pulses.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: NOVA lacks the studied Pacific-salmon subsidy; use prey observations, not calendar dates.

rules.condition: At least 100-150 mm in the salmon-egg study
rules.mechanism: Gape and foraging ability changed prey use.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not convert diet shift into catchability or a generic size bonus.

rules.condition: Observed spawning near 14.4 C in Massachusetts
rules.mechanism: Adults aggregate and construct communal gravel nests.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Spawning and nest aggregation do not prove feeding.

rules.condition: Any universal feeding optimum inferred from spawning, distribution or warming studies
rules.mechanism: No direct temperature-feeding curve qualified.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting season and habitat occupancy.

rules.condition: Any mg/L category
rules.mechanism: No direct feeding/catchability endpoint qualified.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Tolerance or occurrence must not be substituted.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Reject folklore.

rules.condition: Any phase
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer from nighttime angling anecdotes.

rules.condition: Fixed numerical monthly curve
rules.mechanism: No direct monthly per-fish curve.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Separate temperature, spawn, prey and access.

rules.condition: Small flies, jigs, spinners, plugs and live bait
rules.mechanism: Regional agencies document practical intentional targeting.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Not an environmental score input.

rules.condition: Juvenile laboratory fish at <=7 C
rules.mechanism: Cold temperature suppressed juvenile feeding under the tested design.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not transfer a hard adult field cutoff or double count season.

rules.condition: Juvenile laboratory fish below 15 C, especially around 11 C
rules.mechanism: Feeding became rare below 15 C and most fish stopped at 11 C.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Keep categorical and bounded; do not invent a smooth curve.

rules.condition: Juvenile laboratory fish at 19-32 C
rules.direction: increase relative to colder tested treatments
rules.mechanism: Maximum consumption was significantly higher at 19 C and remained elevated through 32 C.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Not an adult optimum and not evidence that extreme field heat improves catchability.

rules.condition: Adult size alone
rules.mechanism: Tag returns varied among size classes and river reaches without one portable pattern.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not import Missouri size bins as a universal NOVA curve.

rules.condition: Availability of fish prey or crayfish
rules.mechanism: Regional prey fields and predator size shaped diet.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Fish Guide/forage context; do not equate diet occurrence with catch rate.

rules.condition: Flood-year category without local prey and temperature controls
rules.mechanism: Flow may alter prey access, fullness and condition, but causal direction was not portable.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting discharge, floodplain access, prey and temperature.

rules.condition: Night versus day based only on telemetry movement
rules.mechanism: Movement timing was measured, not feeding or angling.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: No generic nighttime bite bonus.

rules.condition: Minimal winter movement
rules.mechanism: Low movement cannot be converted into feeding cessation; only juvenile laboratory cold feeding was direct.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Keep movement and feeding endpoints separate.

rules.condition: Tributary use during putative spawn
rules.mechanism: Movement/access was measured, not appetite.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting flow, season and reproduction.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Reject folklore.

rules.condition: Calendar month alone
rules.mechanism: Thermal feeding evidence is laboratory and movement studies are not feeding.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting temperature and spawning.

rules.condition: Age-0 gizzard shad under conditions comparable to the experiment: approximately 5 deg C versus 10-20 deg C
rules.direction: lower feeding activity at 5 deg C; increasing feeding acts across the warmer treatments
rules.mechanism: Controlled feeding observations directly measured temperature effects.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: High risk of double-counting cold stress, season, size, and survival; discrete evidence only, not a smooth curve.

rules.condition: Age-0 fish at 10, 15, and 20 deg C
rules.direction: faster evacuation from 10 to 15 deg C, little additional change from 15 to 20 deg C
rules.mechanism: Measured evacuation times constrain the direction without proving an optimum.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer adult feeding, hook vulnerability, or values between/beyond tested temperatures.

rules.condition: Larval/early juvenile fish where plankton abundance is measured
rules.direction: weak positive tendency in feeding incidence/gut fullness
rules.mechanism: Field feeding success usually rose with food abundance, but correlations were weak and site-dependent.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Food abundance, site position, fish size, and reservoir productivity covary.

rules.condition: Routine field ranges represented in two Missouri reservoirs
rules.mechanism: Feeding incidence and gut fullness were not usually correlated with Secchi depth.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not treat one null study as proof of no effect under all turbidity extremes.

rules.condition: Routine field ranges in the Missouri reservoir study
rules.direction: no additional score beyond the controlled age-0 temperature evidence
rules.mechanism: Field temperature was not usually correlated with feeding success, showing that uncontrolled seasonal field correlations can differ from lab causality.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting temperature via season, prey, and size.

rules.condition: Age-0 size classes 5-29 mm TL
rules.direction: larger age-0 fish showed greater feeding success and diet shifts
rules.mechanism: Ontogenetic development changed feeding efficiency and prey use.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Only apply as forage-ecology context, never as an adult bite modifier.

rules.condition: Below approximately 8 deg C in cages or 1-4 deg C laboratory exposures
rules.direction: no bite-score effect; flag population stress/survival context only
rules.mechanism: The study measured mortality and acclimation failure rather than feeding.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Very high risk of converting a survival threshold into a feeding threshold.

rules.condition: Any environmental condition
rules.direction: do not expose a user-facing hook-and-line bite score
rules.mechanism: Direct feeding science exists, but intentional recreational targetability and catchability evidence do not.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Keep forage-availability implications separate from scoring gizzard shad as a target species.

rules.condition: Juvenile ration x temperature combinations
rules.mechanism: Food and temperature interacted to determine juvenile growth.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Growth is not adult bite; do not derive optimum.

rules.condition: Approximately 25-100 JTU
rules.mechanism: HSI abundance association lacked demonstrated causality and used obsolete units.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not convert JTU to NTU or abundance to feeding.

rules.condition: 4-6 or 14-16 JTU in juvenile aquaria
rules.mechanism: Activity reduction was not statistically significant.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Activity is not feeding and juvenile aquaria limit transfer.

rules.condition: Any oxygen threshold from HSI
rules.mechanism: Key HSI oxygen assumptions were partly surrogate centrarchid evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Related-species evidence cannot score green sunfish.

rules.condition: Recent acclimation temperature
rules.mechanism: Thermal limits and mitochondrial performance changed with acclimation.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Preprint physiology endpoint, not catchability.

rules.condition: Bluegill or other competitors present
rules.mechanism: Competition changed habitat occupancy.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not treat habitat presence as feeding.

rules.condition: Mixed shoreline prey including crayfish
rules.mechanism: Reservoir diet indicates opportunistic feeding.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Original full text not recovered and no rate/catch endpoint.

rules.condition: Short-term hook avoidance or depletion
rules.mechanism: No direct study isolated the effect.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer from electrofishing disturbance.

rules.condition: Any pressure or weather-front category
rules.mechanism: No direct species-specific evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid centrarchid folklore.

rules.condition: Any lunar phase
rules.mechanism: No direct species-specific evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer from generalized light sensitivity.

rules.condition: Sustained recent hook-and-line effort at the same waterbody or area
rules.mechanism: Learned lure avoidance reduces per-fish catchability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not substitute month, fish abundance, or general waterbody popularity for measured recent effort.

rules.condition: Progressive cooling relative to recent acclimation
rules.mechanism: Cold water reduces locomotor performance and voluntary movement without proving complete feeding cessation.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not add a separate winter penalty if temperature already represents the seasonal mechanism.

rules.condition: Prolonged water near 95 F (35 C)
rules.mechanism: Chronic extreme heat was associated with very low feed intake and thermal stress.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid separately stacking summer, thermal stress, and low-oxygen penalties without distinct measurements.

rules.condition: Below approximately 2.0 mg/L in winter habitat
rules.mechanism: Bass avoid severe winter hypoxia and exhibit behavioral responses near this concentration.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Apply to habitat availability or refuge selection, not as proof that all fish in the waterbody stop feeding.

rules.condition: Dawn or twilight
rules.mechanism: Acceleration can peak around crepuscular periods, but the study measured movement rather than feeding or catchability.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not stack dawn, cloud, moon, and visibility bonuses without measured underwater light.

rules.condition: Male actively guarding eggs or fry
rules.mechanism: Territorial aggression and brood defense increase vulnerability near the nest.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not label this feeding, apply it to females, or stack it with a generic spring bonus.

rules.condition: Approximately 50 NTU
rules.mechanism: Age-1 foraging was reduced in the agency-summarized evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not transfer a juvenile feeding response directly to adult hook-and-line catchability.

rules.condition: High enough to expand inundated habitat or reduce shoreline sampling efficiency
rules.mechanism: Fish location, accessible habitat, and capture efficiency can change with discharge.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Never transfer the Neuse River 85 m3/s value to Virginia waters.

rules.condition: Above approximately 5 ppt for freshwater-adapted fish
rules.mechanism: Freshwater-adapted adults may move from unsuitable saline habitat.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Local brackish adaptation varies; this is not a lethal or feeding threshold.

rules.condition: Any nominal solunar phase
rules.mechanism: Observed depth and movement associations were not repeatable and angling catchability was not measured.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Moon phase is an inadequate proxy for actual underwater light and overlaps with season and tides.

rules.condition: Ebb, flood, high, low, or slack tide
rules.mechanism: Regional fish can migrate and use large tidal home ranges, but stage-specific catchability was not measured.

rules.condition: Summer, physically suitable patches under 5 m where benthic prey are demonstrably patchy

rules.condition: Individual cobbles within less than 1 m primary-scale groups

rules.condition: Any universal day or night classification
rules.direction: Zero-weight universal diel bonus; display population conflict instead

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting light, geography, predators, competitors, and season.

rules.condition: Physically suitable erosional reaches
rules.direction: Location context: higher prey reaches may hold more dace
rules.mechanism: Reach-scale abundance correlated with prey, but habitat constrained occupancy.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Abundance is not per-fish feeding or catchability; avoid scoring both prey and habitat.

rules.condition: Cobble/boulder erosional habitat versus depositional sand/silt/debris

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Habitat presence must not become a bite multiplier.

rules.condition: Known benthic-invertebrate diet

rules.condition: Juvenile versus adult habitat

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not transfer larval/juvenile habitat to adult catchability.

rules.condition: Fish Guide only: moving benthic prey or lures may remain detectable in very low light

rules.condition: Shallow faster water with cover beneath substrate in comparable Mid-Atlantic streams

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Habitat presence is not feeding; avoid double-counting current, depth, and substrate.

rules.condition: Calendar autumn or any smooth monthly curve without local prey data

rules.condition: Ordinary flow variability in a comparable stream

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Movement endpoint only.

rules.condition: Very low versus high surface solar radiation in Escanaba Lake

rules.condition: Near full or new moon versus intermediate lunar dates

rules.condition: James River July-August, commonly >25 C
rules.mechanism: Tagged fish were rarely recaptured during the warm-water period.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not convert to a sharp 25 C threshold or stack with seasonal angler-effort and mortality rules.

rules.condition: Dusk compared with dawn/day among successful trips
rules.mechanism: Sparse data suggested higher CPUE at dusk.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Only nine successful dusk trips; no nighttime data.

rules.condition: Live bait or guided trip
rules.mechanism: Technique and expertise changed trip success.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Fish Guide only; skill and trip selection confound.

rules.condition: 19.6-32.6 C after capture
rules.mechanism: Warm-water capture can affect post-release outcomes.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Never convert mortality risk into bite probability.

rules.condition: Local prey type and size
rules.mechanism: Prey selection and diet vary with fish size and prey community.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not infer catch rate without prey abundance and presentation data.

rules.condition: Season and connected habitat
rules.mechanism: Adults make seasonal movements.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Movement and population density are not feeding.

rules.condition: At or above 84 F
rules.mechanism: No original direct feeding experiment verified universal cessation.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Corrects the shallow baseline; avoid false precision.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct portable evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Reject folklore and tiny confounded correlations.

rules.condition: Calendar month alone

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting temperature, movement, effort and stocking.

rules.condition: Summer versus winter in the reviewed Ozark telemetry study

rules.condition: Reviewed Ozark telemetry conditions
rules.direction: context: more movement by day; habitat shifts day/night

rules.condition: Flooded riparian access during high-flow events
rules.mechanism: Velocity refuge/habitat occupancy.

rules.condition: Late winter/early spring migration in the reviewed population

rules.condition: Low-water crossings or similar barriers

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Location feature only; not a bite modifier.

rules.condition: Season, hydrologic period, fish length

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Habitat presence must not become catchability.

rules.condition: Outgoing tide during May-June Potomac sampling

rules.condition: Shallow vegetated low-velocity habitats

rules.condition: Local fish and other prey community

rules.doubleCountingRisk: No prey-density response curve was measured.

rules.condition: Increasing survey catch during invasion growth

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not train a bite model on invasion-era abundance as intrinsic activity.

rules.condition: Acclimation and acute temperature effects

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Metabolism is not voluntary feeding.

rules.condition: Any category
rules.mechanism: No qualifying direct species-specific feeding/catchability evidence.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Reject folklore and surrogate evidence.

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid double counting spawning, tide, temperature, vegetation and effort.

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not double-count with spawn season, shallow habitat, or dawn/dusk; do not apply to cuckolders or females.

rules.condition: Dawn or dusk during the studied reproductive period

rules.condition: Passive bait rather than active presentation
rules.mechanism: Passive methods increased hooking depth.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Fish Guide gear rule, not environmental scoring.

rules.condition: Larger/older parental males early in nesting season

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not treat size or early nesting as higher feeding.

rules.condition: Elevated temperature causing earlier spawning
rules.mechanism: Warm conditions shifted spawning phenology in introduced populations.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not translate to bite optimum; Europe transfer limits.

rules.condition: Shy-bold individual differences

rules.condition: Long-term angling removal

rules.condition: Any pressure, front, or moon category

rules.condition: Turbidity with known prey type, density, and fish size

rules.condition: Any generic short-term suppression period

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not score warm water positively; physiology and ethical fish handling remain separate.

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not proxy underwater light or temperature trend with folklore.

rules.condition: Higher/variable April-June discharge

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not double-count flow with season or growth.

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not convert spawn cues into a bite curve.

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not score movement as feeding.

rules.condition: Mean velocity below 0.13 m/s reported in sympatric sites

rules.condition: Courtship, guarding, alloparental care, or filial cannibalism
rules.mechanism: These studies measured reproductive behavior and egg consumption, not ordinary foraging or hooks.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Very high double-counting risk with season and aggregation.

rules.condition: Any condition without new direct species-specific endpoint evidence
rules.mechanism: Broad searches did not locate portable direct feeding/catchability effects.
rules.doubleCountingRisk: Avoid borrowing from related darters.

rules.condition: Measured underwater illuminance approximately 0.05-1 lx, versus full darkness or brighter treatments

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not double count with time of day, cloud, turbidity or solar radiation; adult/local calibration required.

rules.condition: Dawn/dusk or lower measured solar radiation in a lake fishery

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Time of day is a proxy for underwater light and angler behavior; do not add separate dusk and low-light bonuses.

rules.condition: Lake depth, clarity and thermal structure

rules.condition: Kaw Dam tailwater discharge high enough to entrain or concentrate white crappie

rules.doubleCountingRisk: Do not reuse Oklahoma discharge values or interpret concentration as increased feeding.

rules.mechanism: Photoperiod correlated with exploitation but covaried with discharge, season, effort, temperature, and fish immigration.

rules.condition: Known high-exploitation, high-effort reservoir population

rules.condition: Saltatory searching and life-stage-dependent prey detection

rules.condition: Any direct atmospheric or solunar multiplier
